classification.difficultyReason: Find four exact boundary values and identify two strict solution intervals on an absolute-value graph.

inlines.text: and select where it lies below

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=|x^2-4|$ and $y=3$. Their intersections satisfy
$$\begin{align*}|x^2-4|&=3\\x^2-4&=-3\quad\text{or}\quad x^2-4=3\\x^2&=1\quad\text{or}\quad x^2=7\\x&=\pm1\quad\text{or}\quad x=\pm\sqrt7.\end{align*}$$
The absolute-value graph is below $y=3$ when
$$-\sqrt7<x<-1\quad\text{or}\quad 1<x<\sqrt7.$$
The intersection values are excluded because the inequality is strict.

spec.description: Equation-driven absolute-value graph and horizontal comparison line, with four excluded boundary points.
spec.mathematics: y=|x^2-4| and y=3 intersect at x=-sqrt(7), -1, 1, sqrt(7). The required graph lies below the line in the two inner side intervals.
